summary: Several added docs omit or misstate edge-case behavior of the runtime implementations.

items.issue: The summary says it tests for at least `atLevel` dimensions, but `atLevel <= 0` returns `false` for every array: `isArrayClass` only stops successfully at exactly level 1.
items.suggestion: Document the non-positive-level behavior, or limit the dimensionality claim explicitly to positive `atLevel` values without implying an unenforced constraint.

items.issue: The zero-step `@throws` is incomplete. The returned `NumericRange` also throws `IllegalArgumentException` when its lazily computed length exceeds `Int.MaxValue`; the default-step overload has the same deferred failure.
items.suggestion: State that computing the range length can throw `IllegalArgumentException` for a zero step or for a range with more than `Int.MaxValue` elements, and add the corresponding case to the default-step overload's documentation.

items.issue: The zero-step `@throws` omits the other deferred `NumericRange.length` failure: an `IllegalArgumentException` when the range has more than `Int.MaxValue` elements. The default-step overload omits it too.
items.suggestion: Document both deferred `IllegalArgumentException` conditions for both `to` overloads.

items.issue: `maxElements` is documented as an upper bound, but negative values are accepted and cause `take(maxElements)` to render zero elements; zero is not “at most” a negative bound.
items.suggestion: Document that a negative `maxElements` renders no collection or array elements, or otherwise phrase the bound only for non-negative values while stating the negative case.

items.issue: The documentation omits that, after the cache becomes megamorphic, delegated `MegaMethodCache.find` calls `Class.getMethod` and can throw `NoSuchMethodException` instead of returning `null`.
items.suggestion: Add an `@throws NoSuchMethodException` tag for a megamorphic lookup whose receiver class lacks the required public method.

items.issue: It says every call records `m` and replaces the cache with an extended cache. A `MegaMethodCache.add` returns itself and deliberately records no per-receiver entry, so neither claim holds once the site is megamorphic.
items.suggestion: Describe the operation as replacing the soft reference with `get.add(receiver, m)` and note that a megamorphic cache remains unchanged while `m` is still returned.
